domain: The capability curve itself: trajectory, access and gates

bottlenecks.name: Physical clock: test, fabrication, qualification, launch
bottlenecks.description: Once a math or design result exists, flown change waits on hardware build, integration and test, qualification campaigns (thermal-vacuum, vibration, life tests), supplier lead times (rad-hard parts often 12-24+ months) and launch slots. These sit on the critical path of every space program and compress little under any AI scenario (general).
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~40% of the lag between 'AI can do the math' and 'a space system behaves differently' (judgment, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Limited. Optimal experiment design, better first-pass designs and fewer design escapes can cut test iterations and rework (estimated 10-30%, general), but cannot shorten a 10,000-hour thruster life test, a creep test or a fab cycle.

bottlenecks.name: Access and release governance
bottlenecks.description: The strongest math models are internal or restricted. GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld for deception on Sep 29, 2026; Anthropic's Mythos tier is restricted; US pre-release review adds roughly 12-30 days (GPT-5.6 cleared a 12-day White House gate, Jul 2026); the DC Circuit upheld the DoD 'supply chain risk' designation of Anthropic on Sep 25, 2026; ITAR/CUI and classified data need accredited environments.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: None directly; this is policy, safety and accreditation. Competition among at least four labs and open-weight followers erodes it over time.

bottlenecks.name: Trust and verification bandwidth
bottlenecks.description: Machine checking is cheap but not free (a local Comparator run hit 7 GiB memory caps on two of three openai/math targets); statement audits and human understanding do not scale (722 manuscripts at once; nothing above T3). Engineers will not use a result in a review they cannot trust.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High: autoformalization plus independent AI auditors can cut audit cost from expert-weeks to hours, leaving the human judgment of 'is this the right property'.

bottlenecks.name: Formal infrastructure for applied math
bottlenecks.description: Lean/Mathlib is strong in discrete math and weak in PDE (3 of 16 families formalized), dynamics (2 of 12), numerical analysis and floating point. Applied results therefore stay at T1 and cannot feed formal verification (P2).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High: agents can write library code at scale (FLT: 13.4M lines). The gate is abstraction design and community review bandwidth, not proof labor.

bottlenecks.name: Certification and regulatory acceptance
bottlenecks.description: DO-178C/DO-333/DO-330, NASA software assurance and ECSS give credit to formal methods but not to AI-produced proofs or AI tools; standards change on 5-10 year cycles (general).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Moderate: AI drafts specifications and certification evidence and can be treated as an untrusted generator behind a qualified checker; acceptance remains institutional.

bottlenecks.name: Data for learned and theory models
bottlenecks.description: Space physics is data-poor: one Sun with ~15 years of SDO imagery, few hypersonic flights, sparse thermosphere density data. The weather playbook (ERA5's 40+ years of reanalysis) does not transfer where data cannot be simulated.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-moderate: physics priors, provable identifiability limits and optimal sensor placement; AI cannot create flight data.

bottlenecks.name: Compute and price
bottlenecks.description: Not binding for math: a research-grade result costs ~$200 in tokens (Astra's ten August results ~$2,000 at API rates). Binding for the recursive scenario and for training large emulators (compute stock grows 3.4x/yr; GW-scale sites take ~2.1 years).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Not applicable; this is capital, fabs and power.

nodes.title: Research-grade math inside the labs
nodes.description: Frontier labs' internal models resolve research-level open problems on request, across all of mathematics, at about three hours of compute per result, with agent-written Lean for a large minority of results.
nodes.status_oct2026: Exists. openai/math (Oct 6, 2026): 722 manuscripts, 372 families from ~4,000 posed problems in under four weeks; 127 families carry unchecked agent-written Lean (T3), e.g. 102 Unique Games and 362 relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell. The model was trained from Aug 28, 2026 for about a month. Anthropic (67.2% of zeta zeros on the critical line; full FLT in Lean, Comparator-checked by Buzzard Sep 4) and Google DeepMind (AlphaProof Nexus, 9 Erdos problems, May 2026) are at or near the same level; the gap between labs is months.
nodes.why: About 9% of posed problems survived into result families; cost is roughly three hours of Pro-tier thinking compute per result, and OpenAI put its ten August results at ~$2,000 of tokens (~$200 each). The difficulty ladder moved from IMO gold (Jul 2025) to Erdos-type open problems (spring 2026) to famous conjectures (UGC, forced Navier-Stokes blowup, Sep-Oct 2026) in about 15 months. Every downstream node in the space tree starts here.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Nothing in the release is above T3; the only audit of an earlier OpenAI release covered ten results. The 4,000 problems were chosen by the lab and skew discrete and finitary; PDE (3 of 16 families formalized), dynamics (2 of 12) and topology (1 of 18) are thin, which is where space physics lives. Calegari scored the release at roughly 5 of 100 points on his own list of hard number-theory problems.
nodes.signpost: An independent Comparator run plus statement audit on a headline family (102 or 362) moving it to T4; a published error rate from a random sample of 30 or more families.

nodes.title: Research-grade math for outside teams
nodes.description: An outside engineering team can buy, on demand, mathematics at roughly the October-2026 internal level (journal-grade open problems, proofs with Lean output) through a public or trusted-access product, for under ~$1,000 per result.
nodes.status_oct2026: Partly. Public GPT-6 Astra (paid users from Sep 4, 2026) solved 106 ErdosBench open problems (43 completely) and became the first model to solve any FrontierMath Erdos problem (2 of 68; Epoch, Sep 3, 2026) - research math at the easy end. AlphaEvolve has been generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. The model behind openai/math is unreleased; GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld on Sep 29, 2026; Anthropic's Mythos tier is restricted. OpenAI's ChatGPT for Academic Researchers gives 10,000 researchers free access now and 100,000 by 2027 (Jul 29, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist says the lab does not prioritize math in public models (Sep 10, 2026).
nodes.why: The reveal-to-release lag for Astra was about five weeks (Aug 1 reveal, Sep 4 public), but the most capable versions get held back for safety (GPT-6.1 Astra) or restricted (Mythos), and US pre-release review adds 12-30 days. Under S2 a public model matches the Oct-2026 internal level 6-12 months out (mid-to-late 2027); under S1, 12-18 months (2028). At least four labs compete (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, SpaceXAI with 35-58-day Grok cadence) and open-weight followers trail by about a year, which forces release. The binding gate is release governance (lab safety holds plus government review), coded here as regulatory.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Labs may keep their best math models internal: OpenAI says its urgency is recursive self-improvement and alignment, the Advisory Group asks labs not to test open problems on proprietary models, and dual-use cyber capability (not math) drives the holds. Public models are jagged - strong on discrete Erdos-style problems, weaker on PDE analysis - so an engineering team may get less than the catalog suggests.
nodes.signpost: Any public model scoring 20% or more on FrontierMath Erdos (GPT-6 Astra: 3% in Sep 2026) by end-2027 (S2 on track) versus under 10% (S1); a lab launching a research-math API tier with Lean output.

nodes.title: Agentic Lean formalization at scale
nodes.description: Agents turn informal proofs into Lean and complete them, at the scale of hundreds of papers or a multi-million-line project in weeks.
nodes.status_oct2026: Exists for discrete and algebraic math. openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers by agent (unchecked, T3). Anthropic's FLT formalization (13.4M lines) passed Buzzard's Comparator run (Sep 4, 2026). Meta reportedly autoformalized textbooks into a large Lean library using 183B tokens (May 2026, secondary report). Weak where Mathlib is thin: PDE 3 of 16 families, dynamics 2 of 12, topology 1 of 18.
nodes.why: Lean is hard to fool once the statement is right, and proof labor is no longer scarce: the same pipeline that formalized 162 papers can prove properties of flight algorithms and code (P2). 362 shows agents can build missing PDE infrastructure for a single result. What remains scarce is formal semantics for real code and correct statements.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Coverage is uneven exactly where space needs it (PDE, numerics, stochastic processes). Agent-written Lean can be enormous and slow to check: two of three openai/math targets exceeded a 7 GiB memory cap in an outside run. A proof of the wrong statement is worthless.
nodes.signpost: An agent formalizes a PDE or numerical-analysis paper end to end, including missing library infrastructure, with an outside Comparator pass.

nodes.title: AI does research-grade applied math
nodes.description: Engineers routinely get, from AI, well-posedness and stability analyses of their own models, numerical schemes with certified error bounds, uncertainty quantification with guarantees, and optimal-control results with proofs.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet a routine service. The catalog shows applied-adjacent depth: 362 Vlasov-Maxwell [L, T3]; 363 and 364 Boltzmann (T1); 372 elasticity inverse problem (T1); 365 boundary recovery [L, T3]; plus the separate forced Navier-Stokes blowup claim (Sep 8). These were lab-posed problems, PDE formalization is thin, and nothing in the release touches UQ, stiff numerics or radiation transport.
nodes.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (position a); what it adds is messy context: empirical coefficients, real boundary conditions, and a need for explicit constants and rates. A stability proof for a specific control law or a convergence bound for a specific solver is a week-to-month task for a specialist (general), which fits inside the S2 task horizon by 2027-28. Under S1, diffusion waits on public access (2028) plus domain workflows. This is mostly 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' work, so on-demand expertise is the unlock.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Engineers already get adequate answers from simulation and test without proofs; certified bounds for realistic 3D multiphysics are often too loose to use; the gain is confidence, not performance (position d). Several catalog premises are T1, so implications resting on 363, 364 and 372 are conditional.
nodes.signpost: A NASA, ESA or major-prime technical report, or an AIAA paper, in which an AI-produced stability proof, convergence proof or certified error bound decides a design question.

nodes.title: AI builds validated physics theory
nodes.description: AI derives closures, reduced-order models with proofs, and plasma, materials or combustion theory that beat the human state of the art on held-out experimental data.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet. The catalog touches foundations (364 Boltzmann from Newtonian gases, T1; 278 Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails, T1; 263 ionization bounds [L, T3]), but no AI-built closure has displaced an engineering model. The data-driven precedent is weather: ECMWF's AI forecast system went operational on Feb 25, 2025, beating physics models on many measures (up to 20% on cyclone tracks) at ~1,000x less energy per forecast - an emulator, not new theory.
nodes.why: Theory-building needs month-to-year research horizons (S2: 2028-29) and validation data. Where databases exist (turbulence DNS, DFT databases, plasma experiments) validation is a cognitive task and S2 delivers by 2029; where it needs new experiments, the physical clock binds. Under S3 closed-loop labs supply validation data from ~2028. These are genuinely open problems, unlike most nodes in this tree.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Turbulence and anomalous-transport closures have resisted 60+ years because the missing information is not in the equations; learned closures have historically failed out of distribution. The catalog premises here are T1, so the chain is conditional.
nodes.signpost: An AI-derived closure or reduced model adopted in a production code (NASA FUN3D, US3D, or a major plasma code) after blind validation on data it never saw.

nodes.title: AI multiphysics design with guarantees
nodes.description: AI runs end-to-end multiphysics design optimization (aero-thermal-structural-propulsion) with constraint satisfaction and error bounds, producing designs that pass existing engineering review gates.
nodes.status_oct2026: Early. Generative structural design and AI-generated engine geometry exist (general); AlphaEvolve is generally available for problems with checkable objectives (Jul 9, 2026). Chip design is the leading indicator: Cadence reported a fully autonomous design agent (Jun 2026), Synopsys and AMD launched agents (Oct 2, 2026), and OpenAI-Synopsys announced an EDA-operating model (Oct 6, 2026) - all secondary press reports.
nodes.why: EDA shows the pattern: when the simulator is trusted and the objective is checkable, agents already do weeks of design work. Space multiphysics simulators are less trusted (turbulence, ablation, combustion), so guarantees hold only inside validated envelopes. Under S2, applied math (2027) plus trusted emulators (2028) give design loops by 2028; under S1, 2030.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Design quality is bounded by model fidelity, and optimizers exploit model error. Launch-vehicle performance is set mostly by the rocket equation and propellant chemistry, leaving single-digit percent gains; the hardware still has to be built and tested.
nodes.signpost: A prime or NewSpace firm publicly attributes a flown or hot-fired hardware design (engine, structure, heat shield) to an AI design loop whose model-based margins its review board accepted.

nodes.title: AI-run closed-loop labs at scale
nodes.description: AI plans, runs and interprets experiments on robotic lab hardware, closing design-build-test loops for materials, chemistry and components at 10x or more the throughput of human-run labs.
nodes.status_oct2026: Early. Periodic Labs launched with a $300M seed (Sep 30, 2025); Radical AI and others run self-driving materials labs; DOE's Genesis Mission (~$5B starter allocation, first awards Jul 22, 2026) funds autonomous laboratories at national labs. No space-qualified material has come out of a closed loop yet.
nodes.why: Cognition is not the lab bottleneck; robots, synthesis throughput and characterization are. Under S2 and S3 the planning agent is effectively free, so capital (roughly $10-100M per lab, general) and the physics of synthesis bind. Solution chemistry and thin films speed up most; bulk aerospace materials least.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Superalloys, UHTCs and ablators need furnaces, bulk processing and days per sample; creep, oxidation and radiation tests run in real time (years of creep data cannot be compressed). Qualification, not discovery, sets the insertion timeline for space materials.
nodes.signpost: An autonomous lab reports a new material entering a space-qualification program; Genesis Mission autonomous-lab throughput milestones.

nodes.title: Lean libraries for analysis, PDE and numerics
nodes.description: Mathlib or companion libraries cover Sobolev spaces, weak solutions, standard PDE energy estimates, ODE and numerical-analysis theory, and stochastic processes well enough that applied results formalize routinely.
nodes.status_oct2026: Thin. Mathlib has ~138,000 definitions, ~290,000 theorems and 772 contributors (stats page, accessed Oct 7, 2026). openai/math formalized 3 of 16 PDE families and 2 of 12 dynamics families versus 5 of 6 logic families. 362 [L, T3] shows agents can build what one result needs.
nodes.why: Agents now write library code at FLT scale, so proof labor is not the gate; good abstractions and community review are. Under S2, agent-built applied libraries mature in 2027 and are integrated into Mathlib by 2028; under S1, review bandwidth stretches this to 2030. Every P2 chain that touches continuous physics (GNC stability, plasma, CFD error bounds) waits on this node.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Mathlib's maintainers and review process are the bottleneck and may resist agent-written code; parallel libraries could fragment the ecosystem; formal PDE theory still won't cover the empirical closures engineers actually use.
nodes.signpost: Mathlib or a Lean FRO-backed library merges Sobolev embeddings, Lax-Milgram and standard energy estimates; an applied PDE family from the catalog (363, 364 or 372) receives a Comparator-checked formalization.

nodes.title: Verified floating-point and numerics toolchain
nodes.description: A toolchain that proves floating-point programs and numerical methods (ODE integrators, linear solvers, convex optimizers, filters) meet stated error bounds, from the mathematics down to compiled code.
nodes.status_oct2026: Pieces exist outside Lean - Coq's Flocq and CompCert, Gappa, FPTaylor, Frama-C (general) - but there is no integrated stack and Lean lacks a mature IEEE-754 plus numerical-analysis library. The catalog contains no numerics results, and the release does not touch numerical analysis of stiff systems.
nodes.why: Verified numerics is solved in principle but expert-scarce: a round-off and truncation analysis of a GNC loop takes a specialist weeks to months (general). Agents that already write millions of lines of Lean remove the labor; integration with existing Coq tools or a Lean port is a 1-2 year engineering job under S2.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Proofs on real flight code stall on compiler semantics, nonstandard FPUs on rad-hard processors and environment models, not on the numerics; many GNC teams already use fixed-point or conservative margins that make the proof unnecessary.
nodes.signpost: An agent-generated, machine-checked round-off bound for a flight Kalman filter or guidance law reported by NASA, ESA, AdaCore, Galois or a prime.

nodes.title: Regulators accept AI-produced proofs
nodes.description: Certification authorities (FAA via DO-178C, DO-333 and DO-330; NASA software assurance; ECSS; Space Force) grant credit for formal proofs produced by AI agents, with a qualified proof checker as the trusted base.
nodes.status_oct2026: No credit yet for AI-generated proofs. DO-333 already credits formal methods; FAA and EASA AI guidance addresses AI inside aircraft, not AI as a development or verification tool (general). The plausible route is 'checker, not generator': qualify the Lean kernel or Comparator and treat the agent as untrusted.
nodes.why: Aviation software standards turn over on 5-10+ year cycles (DO-178B 1992, DO-178C 2011), but the checker route needs no new standard: DO-330 already qualifies tools, and a small proof kernel is a better qualification target than any test tool. Under S2, first project-level credit lands in 2029-30. Capped at Medium because it needs regulator acceptance.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Regulators move slowly and specifications become the bottleneck. Uncrewed commercial space needs no software certification at all, so this gate matters mainly for crewed vehicles, aviation-adjacent systems and NASA human-rating.
nodes.signpost: An FAA issue paper, NASA project or ESA mission accepting Lean-checked proofs as verification evidence; a DO-330 qualification kit for a Lean checker.

nodes.title: Independent checks of AI math
nodes.description: Outside groups run Comparator on the labs' Lean challenges and audit formal statements against the manuscripts, moving key results from T3 to T4.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet for any openai/math family. Kingy AI (Oct 6, 2026) ran Comparator on three challenge targets on an 8 GiB VM: one passed twice, two hit a 7 GiB memory cap; same operator, no statement audit, so no tier change. Hexagon launched Oct 6 (beta; Buzzard on its advisory board) but does not require formalization and holds no OpenAI deposits yet. Precedent: Buzzard's Comparator run on Anthropic's FLT (Sep 4, 2026).
nodes.why: A Comparator run needs hours and a large-memory machine; the statement audit needs a domain expert for days per family. Headline Lean families (102, 362) should reach T4 within one to three months; the long tail of 127 formalized families and the 245 unformalized ones takes years. Under S2, AI-assisted statement audits speed the tail.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Human bandwidth is the limit: a few dozen qualified readers per field and 722 manuscripts at once. Independent machine checks confirm only formal statements, and statement gaps already exist (the quasi-RH challenge targets zeta only).
nodes.signpost: Hexagon, Buzzard's group or another expert team publishes a Comparator pass plus statement audit for 102 or 362.

nodes.title: Month-long autonomous research tasks
nodes.description: AI agents complete, at 50% reliability or better, technical research tasks that take a human expert a full work-month (~170 hours), up from about a work-week in late 2026.
nodes.status_oct2026: METR measured frontier 50% time horizons of ~16-20 hours in Feb-Mar 2026 and says its suite cannot reliably measure above ~16 hours (Frontier Risk Report, May 19, 2026); GPT-5.6 Sol was ~11.3 hours (95% CI 5-40, flagged unreliable; Jun 26, 2026). Long-run doubling ~7 months since 2019, ~4 months in 2024-25 (METR, Jul 14, 2025). In mathematics the internal model returns, in ~3 hours of compute, results that take experts weeks to months.
nodes.why: Parametrization: start at ~40 h (one work-week) in Oct 2026, one 7-month doubling past the measured 16-20 h. S1 doubles every 12-18 months: ~76 h end-2027, ~230 h end-2029, ~700 h end-2031 (~4 work-months). S2 doubles every 6-9 months: ~150 h end-2027 (range 120-200), ~1,300 h end-2029, ~12,000 h end-2031 (2-26 work-years across the 6-9 month range). S3 follows S2 to end-2027 then doubles every ~3 months, so the metric stops being meaningful around 2029. The month threshold is the point where a whole applied-math project (model, analysis, proof, code) fits in one autonomous run.
nodes.strongest_case_small: METR suites saturate and measure well-specified software tasks; research is open-ended and judgment-heavy; 80%-reliability horizons are several times shorter than 50% horizons, and engineering needs high reliability. Capability is jagged across domains.
nodes.signpost: A successor horizon suite (METR or Epoch) reporting a frontier 50% horizon of 80 hours or more by end-2027 (S2 on track) or under 40 hours (S1).

nodes.title: AI speeds up its own development 3x
nodes.description: AI systems accelerate frontier AI research and engineering, including chip design and software stacks, by 3x or more overall - the hinge between S2 and S3.
nodes.status_oct2026: METR estimates ~1.5x acceleration during Claude Opus 5.5's development, a ~30% chance of 2x, and judges it unlikely to fully automate AI R&D (Sep 22, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist names recursive self-improvement and automated alignment research as priorities (Sep 10, 2026). Agentic EDA (Cadence, Synopsys, OpenAI-Synopsys) applies the same loop to chips.
nodes.why: Software-side acceleration is bounded by compute for experiments. Epoch: frontier training compute grows ~5x/yr, compute stock ~3.4x/yr, GW-scale sites take ~2.1 years at ~$38B per GW; Anthropic alone lists ~$518B of decade-long compute obligations. S3 assumes acceleration past 3x by 2028 converts into ~10x/yr effective efficiency gains, collapsing the cost of cognitive work; even then the recursion runs on fabs and power, which are a physical clock.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Amdahl's law inside AI labs: experiments need GPUs, and CoWoS, HBM and power supply chains are physical. METR reports weak judgment and foresight. Safety holds (GPT-6.1 Astra) and government review slow deployment even when capability races ahead.
nodes.signpost: Lab system cards or METR reporting 2x+ uplift with high confidence; frontier release cadence under 30 days across several labs; AI-designed accelerator tape-outs.

nodes.title: A research result costs less than an engineer-day
nodes.description: The public price of a research-grade math result (problem posed to checked proof or derivation) falls below ~$1,000 and then below ~$100, cheaper than one day of a specialist's time.
nodes.status_oct2026: Internally ~3 hours of Pro-tier compute per result; OpenAI put Astra's ten August results at ~$2,000 at API rates (~$200 each). GPT-6 Astra is public in ChatGPT and the API (Sep 2026), with a new $500/month Pro tier and a cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol reported as near-Astra at a fifth of the price (press). Epoch: price for a fixed capability level fell 9-900x per year in 2022-25; AI chip price-performance improves ~49%/yr.
nodes.why: At ~$200 per result, a space program posing 1,000 hard analysis problems a year spends ~$0.2M - less than one engineer. Illustratively, an Oct-2026-grade result falls to ~$20-70 by 2028 in S1 (3-10x/yr) and ~$1-10 in S2. Price stops being a gate for math in every scenario; access, trust and integration remain.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The cost of checking dominates the cost of producing: a $200 proof that needs a $20,000 expert audit is a $20,000 result. Frontier tasks get longer, so spend per frontier task may stay flat even as fixed-capability prices fall.
nodes.signpost: Lab price sheets for long-horizon reasoning tiers; enterprise contracts that bundle research math with Lean output; space-firm disclosures of AI analysis spend.

nodes.title: Frontier math on ITAR and classified networks
nodes.description: Research-grade models run inside ITAR/EAR-compliant, CUI and classified environments, so space primes, Space Force and NRO programs can pose problems with export-controlled engineering data.
nodes.status_oct2026: GenAI.mil reached ~3M DoD personnel with a ChatGPT-based 'ChatGPT Mil', Grok and Gemini (Fortune, Sep 1, 2026; ~500,000 power users per DefenseScoop, Sep 23); OpenAI, Google, xAI and others were cleared for classified networks (May 2026). The DoD designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk, upheld by the DC Circuit on Sep 25, 2026, barring contractors from using Claude on DoD work - the lab behind the only Comparator-checked mega-formalization (FLT). Civil NASA is unaffected: JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives (Dec 2025).
nodes.why: Much space engineering data (propulsion, GNC, hypersonics, defense payloads) is ITAR-controlled, and P1 works best when teams pose problems with real data. Accredited government clouds have trailed commercial releases by months (general). No US export control restricts API access to closed models today; controls target chips (general), and policy can still remove a lab overnight.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The math itself is not controlled: engineers can pose sanitized problems without technical data. Defense adoption is limited by security culture and model-weight custody more than availability. Policy volatility cuts both ways.
nodes.signpost: A research-math-capable model accredited at IL6 or Top Secret; a change to the Anthropic designation; State Department or DDTC guidance on AI processing of ITAR technical data.

nodes.title: Open-weight model at research-math level
nodes.description: An open-weight model matches the October-2026 internal research-math level, removing lab release decisions and access controls as a gate for everyone, including adversaries.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet. Press frames Moonshot's Kimi K3 as Astra's competitor (Aug 2026); the US threatened to blacklist Moonshot over distillation (Jul 22, 2026). Open models have historically trailed the closed frontier by about a year (general).
nodes.why: With a ~12-month open-weight lag, the Oct-2026 internal level reaches open weights in late 2027 to 2028 under S2. For space this matters two ways: on-premises use with ITAR data without cloud accreditation, and competitors and adversaries getting the same on-demand math for trajectory design, constellation tasking and weapons-relevant analysis.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Open models may lag more at the frontier of math reasoning (RL compute is expensive), and distillation crackdowns could widen the gap; most engineering math does not need the frontier anyway.
nodes.signpost: An open-weight model solving FrontierMath Erdos problems or matching GPT-6 Astra's ErdosBench score.

nodes.title: AI cryptanalysis of space-link crypto (watch item)
nodes.description: An AI-produced result materially weakens a standardized primitive used in satellite command and data links (lattice schemes such as ML-KEM, elliptic curves, or AES modes), forcing re-keying or hardware upgrades on long-lived spacecraft.
nodes.status_oct2026: Nothing in openai/math breaks deployed cryptography: 279 (exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set, T1) is theory only and does not cut qubit budgets; 272 and 266 refine quantum-key-distribution theory. One of Astra's ten August problems was in lattice cryptography, with no reported effect on deployed schemes. Models' demonstrated strength is implementation bugs and historical ciphers, not number-theoretic breaks.
nodes.why: Satellites fly 5-15 years with fixed cryptographic implementations and limited on-orbit agility (general). Even a non-practical weakening (say, tens of bits off a lattice parameter set) would trigger costly re-keying and upgrade programs. Research-grade AI math pointed at LWE, isogenies or discrete log is the channel; this node tracks it, it does not predict it.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Decades of human cryptanalysis; standardized parameter sets carry wide margins; AI's track record is bugs, not breaks. A software vulnerability is far likelier than a mathematical one and is a cybersecurity issue, not a math one.
nodes.signpost: Any AI-lab result on LWE, SIS, isogenies or discrete log; a NIST or NSA reassessment of post-quantum parameter margins.

nodes.title: Trust in hours: automated statement audits
nodes.description: AI-assisted pipelines check that a formal statement matches the engineering claim (definitions, hypotheses, units, scope), cross-check proofs with independent agents and produce human-readable audit trails, cutting the cost of trusting an AI result from expert-weeks to hours.
nodes.status_oct2026: Statement gaps are real: openai/math's quasi-RH challenge targets only zeta; the outside run of the Pi Exponent target found its formal statement omits a manuscript consequence. Human review does not scale to 722 manuscripts. AGMAI (Sep 29) and the Simons Institute report (Sep 28) call for disclosure and lineage norms.
nodes.why: In engineering, statement gaps become specification errors, the main residual risk in formally verified systems (general). An adversarial auditor model plus Lean plus a human sign-off turns P1 answers into evidence a design review can accept. This is the node that moves the bottleneck from proving to understanding (position h) back toward engineering.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Generator and auditor models can share blind spots; the final judgment of whether a property is the right one is irreducibly human and domain-specific.
nodes.signpost: Hexagon or a journal adopting AI-assisted statement audits as standard; a NASA or ESA review board accepting an AI audit trail.

nodes.title: AI-discovered algorithms in space codes
nodes.description: AlphaEvolve-style search (a model proposes code, an automatic evaluator scores it) improves practical heuristics and kernels used in space operations and engineering: constellation scheduling, conjunction screening, trajectory solvers, onboard compression, CFD kernels.
nodes.status_oct2026: AlphaEvolve's scheduling heuristic recovers ~0.7% of Google's fleet compute, a kernel sped up 23% (1% off Gemini training time) and FlashAttention up to 32.5% (May 14, 2025); generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. Unlike the catalog's galactic speedups (107, 130 - no practical gain), these have practical constants. Hardness results (102, 117, 125, all [L], T3) mark where general-purpose gains are capped.
nodes.why: It needs only an evaluator function, which space operations have (schedule value, screening runtime, compression ratio). For a 10,000-satellite constellation, a few percent of tasking or ground-contact efficiency is worth tens of millions of dollars a year (general). The hardness results (P3) tell teams to stop chasing general solvers and invest in instance structure, which is exactly what evolutionary search exploits.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Gains are incremental (single-digit percent); structured instances already solve well with commercial MIP solvers; worst-case ceilings say little about real instances.
nodes.signpost: A constellation operator or space agency publishing an AI-discovered heuristic in production with measured gains.

nodes.title: Trusted AI emulators of space physics codes
nodes.description: The weather-model playbook - train on decades of simulation or reanalysis data, run ~1,000x cheaper - applied to space codes (CFD and aerothermal, plasma, thermosphere, structures), with calibrated uncertainty or certified error bounds supplied by AI applied math.
nodes.status_oct2026: Weather: ECMWF's AIFS operational Feb 25, 2025, up to 20% better on some measures at ~1,000x less energy, though at 28 km versus 9 km grid spacing. Space: NASA and IBM released the open Surya heliophysics model (Aug 20, 2025; 16% better flare classification, nine years of SDO data) and SuryaBench (Mar 2026). CFD surrogates are common in design exploration but not trusted for margins (general).
nodes.why: Emulators remove the compute cost of design loops and ensembles. Weather moved from research models to operations in about 15 months on the back of 40+ years of reanalysis. Space domains split: where training data can be generated by simulation (CFD, structures, thermal) emulators are data-unconstrained and arrive first; where data come only from nature (one Sun, rare extreme storms, few hypersonic flights) they arrive late and extrapolate poorly.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Emulators are only as good as their training data, and extrapolation to new vehicles or extreme storms - exactly where margins matter - is where they fail. Coarser resolution (as with AIFS) can hide local extremes such as peak heating.
nodes.signpost: NOAA SWPC or ESA running an AI model in operations; a launch provider using a surrogate with stated error bounds in flight-readiness analysis.

nodes.title: On-demand applied math in space engineering
nodes.description: Space engineering organizations routinely pose their own hard analysis problems (stability, bounds, convergence, inverse problems, trade studies) to frontier models and use the checked answers in design reviews.
nodes.status_oct2026: Early. JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives with human review (Dec 2025); NASA and IBM ran a compressed model on the ISS (May 2026); IEEE Spectrum reports engineers' distrust of non-deterministic outputs (Sep 28, 2026). SpaceX owns a frontier lab (SpaceXAI; Grok releases every 35-58 days) and says its Grok bot will route tasks to the best model, including Claude Opus 5.5 (Oct 7, 2026).
nodes.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems: a specialist analysis that takes 2-8 weeks (general) becomes hours plus a check. Vertically integrated firms that own both models and hardware (SpaceX/SpaceXAI) adopt first; primes constrained by ITAR and DoD rules follow 6-12 months later; agencies last.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Analysis is rarely on a space program's critical path; answers still need checking; legacy processes, roles and liability slow uptake; AI may expand analysis scope rather than speed programs.
nodes.signpost: A major prime or NASA center publishing standard work for AI-derived analysis; AIAA papers where an AI-derived proof or bound is used in a flight design.

nodes.title: AI-designed radiation-tolerant space processor
nodes.description: Agentic EDA designs and formally verifies a radiation-tolerant processor or SoC for space (triple modular redundancy, error correction, upset-aware layout); it is taped out and radiation-tested.
nodes.status_oct2026: Agentic chip design is moving fast in commercial EDA (Cadence autonomous agent, Jun 2026; Synopsys and AMD agents, Oct 2, 2026; OpenAI-Synopsys, Oct 6, 2026; all secondary reports). Space processors lag commercial nodes by roughly a decade (general).
nodes.why: Design and verification (12-24 months for a rad-hard SoC, general) compress several-fold; fabrication (3-4 months per run), scarce heavy-ion beam time and QML-class qualification (1-2 years) do not. First tape-out in 2029-30 under S2; flight qualification after 2031.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Space is moving to COTS processors with system-level mitigation, the rad-hard market is small, and qualification rather than design sets the schedule.
nodes.signpost: A rad-hard SoC tape-out credited mainly to agentic EDA, with published heavy-ion test results.

nodes.title: Spacecraft engineered mostly by AI flies
nodes.description: An operational spacecraft whose design analyses, trade studies and flight-software verification artifacts were majority AI-generated (with human review) reaches orbit and operates.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet. Ingredients exist piecemeal: AI-generated engine and structural geometry, agentic coding, JPL drive planning, agentic chip design.
nodes.why: Chain: adoption (S2 2028) -> smallsat design and build in 12-18 months -> rideshare launch -> operations by 2029-30. A small company with no legacy process is the likely first mover; the binding gates are integration, test and a launch slot, not cognition. This is a process outcome, not a performance claim.
nodes.strongest_case_small: It changes who does the engineering, not what flies: performance gains are small, 'majority AI-generated' is hard to verify, and the first claims will be marketing.
nodes.signpost: A company or agency announcing such a mission with published AI-generated verification evidence, followed by on-orbit success.

nodes.title: Development cycles shrink by a third, not 10x
nodes.description: Development time for new space systems (concept to launch) falls by roughly 30-40% under S2 (about 50% under S3, 10-20% under S1), bounded by Amdahl's law because fabrication, integration and test, qualification and launch dominate the critical path.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet. Major NASA projects routinely run late, mostly in hardware, integration and test (GAO reporting, general).
nodes.why: Illustrative critical-path shares (general): requirements and trades 10%, design and analysis 15%, software 10%, fabrication and procurement 25%, integration and test 25%, qualification and reviews 10%, launch campaign 5%. Speedups of 5-10x on cognitive work and 1.1-1.2x on physical work (S2) give a 1.6x overall speedup, a ~38% shorter schedule; S3 (20-50x cognitive, 1.3-1.5x physical) gives ~2x, ~51%; S1 (2x cognitive) gives ~18%. Fewer design escapes found in test cut rework, a second-order gain. Only programs started after adoption (2028+) show it, so evidence appears in 2030-31. Capped at Medium because flown evidence needs qualification.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Schedules are set by funding profiles, supply chains (rad-hard parts 12-24+ months), launch manifests and politics; teams may spend the gain on more analysis and scope (Jevons) instead of shorter schedules.
nodes.signpost: A GAO, ESA or company schedule analysis attributing cycle-time reduction to AI; smallsat build times falling below 9 months for new designs.

scenario_contrast: S1 Plateau (task-horizon doubling every 12-18 months): the Oct-2026 internal level reaches outside teams in 2028, research-grade applied math in 2029, multiphysics design optimization in 2030, applied Lean libraries in 2030; validated physics theory and regulator credit for AI proofs slip past 2031. By 2031 the autonomous horizon is ~4 work-months (~16x today). Space effects are P1 consulting-style analysis, P3 ceilings and AlphaEvolve-type heuristics; new programs run 10-20% shorter. S2 Exponential, base case (doubling every 6-9 months, matching METR's ~7-month long-run trend): public access in 2027, applied math in 2027, applied Lean libraries and verified numerics in 2028, design optimization and autonomous labs at scale in 2028, physics theory in 2029, first certification credit in 2030; horizon ~1 work-month by end-2027 and several work-years by 2031. The cognitive clock runs 10-50x faster by 2029, but fabrication, test, qualification and launch compress only 1.1-1.3x, so new programs are ~30-40% shorter and flown evidence appears only in 2030-31. S3 Recursive (S2 until 2028, then ~3-month doubling once AI speeds its own R&D 3x or more): cognitive work is near-free from ~2029 and closed-loop labs compress materials and chemistry iteration, but launch, flight test, qualification and fabs still bind; programs are at most ~50% shorter, and the recursion itself is bounded by compute supply (stock ~3.4x/yr, ~2.1 years per GW-scale site). Across all three, the biggest difference is how many design iterations and how much verification each program buys - not launch cadence, propellant chemistry or the physics of space.
key_insights: Two clocks: under S2 the cognitive clock doubles every 6-9 months while the physical clock (test, fab, qualification, launch) barely moves, so Amdahl's law caps schedule compression for new space programs at ~30-40% (S2) and ~50% (S3), not 10x.

Price is not the gate: a research-grade result costs ~$200 in tokens (Astra's ten August results ~$2,000), so 1,000 hard problems a year cost less than one engineer. The gates are access, trust and integration.

Public models already do research math at the easy end (GPT-6 Astra: 106 ErdosBench open problems, first ever FrontierMath Erdos solves), so the P1 channel opens in late 2026 for ordinary engineering math; catalog-level capability is 6-12 months away under S2.

Access is governed, not just priced: Astra went from reveal to public in ~5 weeks, but GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld, Anthropic's top tier is restricted, US pre-release review adds 12-30 days, and the DoD bars contractors from using Claude on defense work - removing the lab with the only Comparator-checked mega-formalization from defense-space workflows.

For space, ITAR/CUI and classified accreditation is the binding access gate for real engineering data; open-weight models at research level (2028 in S2) would bypass it for both US firms and adversaries.

Formal infrastructure for continuous math is the gating infrastructure for the formal-verification bridge: PDE 3 of 16 and dynamics 2 of 12 families formalized versus logic 5 of 6; applied Lean libraries arrive ~2028 in S2 and verified numerics alongside.

Verification has moved from proving to auditing: a laptop-class Comparator run of three openai/math targets passed one and ran out of memory on two, and the statement gaps found so far are scope gaps - cheap AI-assisted statement audits are the unlock that lets engineers use AI results in reviews.
The weather playbook transfers first where training data can be simulated (CFD, structures, thermal) and last where nature is the only source (space weather from one Sun, rare hypersonic flights).

Practical algorithm discovery (AlphaEvolve: 0.7% of Google's fleet compute recovered, generally available since Jul 2026) and hardness ceilings act within the window; the catalog's galactic speedups (107, 130) never will.

The shortest path from AI math to flown hardware runs through firms that own both a frontier lab and the launch manifest (SpaceX/SpaceXAI), then new entrants without legacy processes; agencies and crewed programs come last because of qualification.
nil_effects: Launch physics: the rocket equation, propellant energy density and structural mass fractions do not change; AI design optimization yields single-digit percent gains in launch performance.
Durations set by physics or time: thermal-vacuum and vibration campaigns, 10,000+ hour electric-thruster life tests, creep and oxidation tests, battery cycling, radiation beam tests.
Fabrication and supply-chain lead times (rad-hard parts often 12-24+ months, wafer runs, large forgings) and launch-manifest slots, even under S3.
Galactic speedups (107 matrix-multiplication exponent, 130 FFT below n log n) give no practical gain to onboard or ground compute.
Positive well-posedness results (e.g. 362 Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) change confidence in plasma codes, not the codes or thruster performance.
Deployed cryptography: nothing in the release (279 is theory only) weakens space-link crypto; the capability is a watch item, not an effect.
Data scarcity in space physics: one Sun with ~15 years of SDO data, few extreme storms, few instrumented hypersonic flights; AI cannot create flight data.
Standards cycles: DO-178C-class standards turn over on 5-10+ year cycles, so certification credit for AI proofs stays capped at Medium likelihood by 2031 in every scenario.
Compute for the recursive scenario: fabs, HBM, packaging and power (GW-scale sites ~2.1 years) bound S3's own acceleration.
Price of math: already near zero relative to engineering labor, so further price falls change little.

signposts.event: Independent Comparator run plus statement audit published for a headline family (102 Unique Games or 362 Vlasov-Maxwell) by Hexagon, Buzzard's group or similar, Q4 2026 to Q1 2027.
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves those results to T4 and validates the pipeline; a failed audit would downgrade every T3 premise in the tree and lengthen trust timelines.

signposts.event: A public model (any lab) scores 20% or more on FrontierMath Erdos or the Open Problems benchmark by end-2027 (GPT-6 Astra: 3% in Sep 2026).
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms S2 public access in 2027; under 10% by end-2027 points to S1 and pushes every P1 node out by about a year.

signposts.event: A successor task-horizon suite reports a frontier 50% horizon of 80 hours or more by end-2027, or under 40 hours.
signposts.what_it_changes: Discriminates S2 (6-9 month doubling) from S1 (12-18 months); sets the dates for applied math, physics theory and design optimization.

signposts.event: Mathlib or a Lean FRO-backed library merges Sobolev-space, weak-solution and energy-estimate infrastructure; an applied PDE family (363, 364 or 372) is formalized and checked.
signposts.what_it_changes: Opens the formal-verification bridge for continuous physics (GNC stability, plasma, CFD error bounds) on the S2 schedule (2028).

signposts.event: A research-math-capable model accredited at IL6 or Top Secret, or a change to the Anthropic supply-chain-risk designation.
signposts.what_it_changes: Sets when defense-space programs and primes can use the capability with real data; determines which labs' verification tools reach defense space.

signposts.event: First certification credit (FAA, NASA or ESA) for an AI-produced formal proof checked by a qualified proof checker.
signposts.what_it_changes: Pulls infra-tool-qualification forward from 2030 (S2) and unlocks proof-backed crewed and aviation-adjacent software.

signposts.event: A lab or METR reports 2x or more AI R&D uplift with high confidence, or frontier release cadence falls below 30 days across several labs.
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves the base case toward S3 (recursion from ~2028).

signposts.event: Any AI-lab result on LWE, SIS, isogenies or discrete log.
signposts.what_it_changes: Activates the cryptography watch item: crypto-agility requirements for long-lived spacecraft and ground segments.
